title: Remediate BERTopic transitive vulnerabilities via direct dependency upgrades

comments.author: derek.norrbom
comments.text: Start remediation for Snyk findings introduced through bertopic path. Plan: raise direct constraints (bertopic/docling where needed), regenerate lock, run dependency audit, and verify vulnerable packages resolve to fixed versions without transitive pinning.

comments.author: derek.norrbom
comments.text: Implemented source-level dependency remediation and regenerated lockfile. Updated direct constraints: bertopic>=0.17.4, docling/docling-mlx>=2.84.0, and project Python support to >=3.10,<3.14 (to eliminate vulnerable torch 2.7.1 branch tied to py3.14 lock resolution). Resolved lock now includes transformers 5.5.0, aiohttp 3.13.5, torch 2.11.0, torchvision 0.26.0, litellm 1.83.3. Verified with poetry check and osv-scanner lockfile scan; target findings no longer appear.

comments.author: derek.norrbom
comments.text: Second pass started for remaining Snyk findings (transformers/torch). Will verify each Snyk ID for fixed versions and attempt source-level upgrades; if no upstream fix is available, will document best-practice triage rationale.

comments.author: derek.norrbom
comments.text: User granted temporary Snyk CLI auth. Running direct snyk test against lockfile to validate fixable versions for remaining transformers/torch findings before any further dependency changes.

comments.author: derek.norrbom
comments.text: Investigating persistent PATH setup so snyk and similar CLIs are available in Codex non-interactive login shells. Will patch zsh startup files and verify with fresh shell invocation.

comments.author: derek.norrbom
comments.text: Installed Homebrew formula snyk-cli (v1.1303.2). Verified in both current and fresh login shells: command -v snyk -> /opt/homebrew/bin/snyk and snyk --version -> 1.1303.2. This removes dependency on npx/nvm path for Codex shells.

comments.author: derek.norrbom
comments.text: Continuing dependency scan work: running authenticated Snyk CLI scans against poetry.lock/pyproject.toml to replicate console-reported findings and gather exact vulnerability IDs for remediation.

comments.author: derek.norrbom
comments.text: Investigating discrepancy between Snyk web pyproject-only findings and local lockfile scans. Verifying pyproject constraints and lock-resolved versions for pygments/docs stack and bertopic chain to determine if manifest resolution drift is causing findings.

comments.author: derek.norrbom
comments.text: Reproduced web findings locally by including dev dependency graph: snyk test --file=poetry.lock --package-manager=poetry --org=capacity-aqa --dev. Result: 31 vulnerable paths, 15 unique IDs. Breakdown: pygments@2.19.2 (1 fixable ID repeated across 10 paths) plus torch@2.11.0 (7 IDs, no fix) and transformers@5.5.0 (7 IDs, no fix).

comments.author: derek.norrbom
comments.text: Analyzing pygments transitive source chains and whether parent dependency upgrades can remediate without adding a direct pygments pin.

comments.author: derek.norrbom
comments.text: Verified pygments parent constraints via poetry dependency trees. Current parents already match Snyk's suggested versions (pytest 9.0.2, sphinx 8.1.3, python-semantic-release 10.5.3, myst-parser 4.0.1, sphinx-rtd-theme 3.1.0) and still allow vulnerable pygments because they declare wide ranges (e.g., sphinx>=2.17, rich>=2.13,<3). Parent upgrades alone are insufficient; remediation requires explicit pygments>=2.20.0 constraint or waiting for upstream parents to tighten lower bounds.

comments.author: derek.norrbom
comments.text: Applied remediatable fix: added direct dependency floor pygments>=2.20.0 to project dependencies and updated lockfile (pygments 2.19.2 -> 2.20.0). Re-ran Snyk with dev graph: findings dropped from 31 paths / 15 unique IDs to 21 paths / 14 unique IDs. Remaining findings are only torch@2.11.0 (7 IDs, no fix) and transformers@5.5.0 (7 IDs, no fix).

comments.author: derek.norrbom
comments.text: Completed: installed standalone snyk-cli, reproduced web findings with --dev scan, remediated the fixable finding via pygments>=2.20.0 and lockfile update, and validated reduction from 31 paths/15 IDs to 21 paths/14 IDs. Remaining vulnerabilities are no-fix upstream issues in torch/transformers and are tracked in blbs-a7a77d.
